page_title: tarfile — Read and write tar archive files

sources.entry: tarfile - (Python standard library) Read and write tar archives, including gzip, bz2, lzma, and zstd compressed ones.

summary.name: tarfile
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module for reading and writing tar archives, including gzip, bz2, lzma, and Zstandard compressed ones.
use_cases: Creating tar.gz or tar.xz archives from Python scripts
Extracting tar archives safely with extraction filters
Listing the contents of a tar archive
Streaming tar data through stdin, sockets or tape devices
Producing reproducible gzip-compressed archives with mtime 0
Reading concatenated or damaged tar archives
summary.what_it_does: The tarfile module reads and writes tar archives with gzip, bz2, lzma (xz) and Zstandard compression when the corresponding modules are available. It supports the ustar, GNU and pax tar formats and handles regular files, directories, hard and symbolic links, fifos, and device files, preserving timestamps, permissions and owners. Archives can be opened with tarfile.open() in random-access or streaming modes, and members can be listed, extracted (individually or all at once), or added with optional filters. Extraction uses filters; since Python 3.14 the default filter is 'data', which blocks some dangerous features such as absolute-path links.
notable: Part of the Python standard library, so no installation is needed
Extraction filters (data, fully_trusted) guard against unsafe members
Streaming modes ('r|gz', 'w|xz') for stdin, sockets and tape devices
caveats: Compression support for gzip, bz2, zstd depends on the optional modules being present in the Python build
Zstandard compression requires Python 3.14 or later; extraction defaults changed in 3.12 and 3.14
Archives from untrusted sources should be inspected before extraction, per the page's warnings
